How to use Lemon Connect Cameroon

For citizens who want to understand their connection, students and engineers who want to experiment, entrepreneurs planning a telecom business, and decision-makers looking for sourced options.

Open Lemon Connect Cameroon ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to lemon-connect-cameroon.vercel.app.

2

On the first visit, pick a path: curious citizen, student or engineer, entrepreneur, or public decision-maker. Explore alone closes the window.

3

Comment utiliser cette page under each title, or Guide at the top, starts the tour of the page.

4

Words with a dotted underline show their definition on hover, or on tap on a phone.

5

EN switches the whole site to English; Citoyen and Ingénieur change the level of detail.

6

Modules at the top right lists every page.

02

Features

01

Paths and guided tours

Four paths lead each kind of visitor through the pages that matter to them, in order, with a banner showing the step. On every page, the guided tour lights up each part in turn and says what to do with it.

STEPS

  1. Pick a path on the welcome screen, or open Guide
  2. Move with Suivant or the arrow keys
  3. At the last step, go to the next page of the path
02

Definitions on hover

139 technical terms, from latency and backhaul to IXP, spectrum and Cournot, are underlined with dots wherever they appear. Hovering or tapping shows a short definition, with a link to the full glossary, searchable by word and category.

STEPS

  1. Hover or tap a dotted word
  2. Click Glossaire complet for the whole list
  3. Turn the underlining off in the menu if you prefer
03

A packet's journey

A request from a phone in Douala crosses the antenna, the backhaul, the national backbone, the core network, DNS, the content cache and the server. Each piece of equipment shows its load, what it does, what it costs, what can break and who runs it. Faults can be switched on, then repaired.

STEPS

  1. Click a piece of equipment on the path
  2. Switch on a fault in Provoquer une panne
  3. Click Réparer cette connexion
04

The 4G and 5G lab

Subscribers, peak hour, spectrum, sectors, MIMO and signal quality are sliders. The lab computes the speed each user gets and names the point that limits it: the radio, the backhaul or the international link.

STEPS

  1. Choose a place, from a Douala neighbourhood to a village
  2. Move the sliders
  3. Read which link limits the speed
05

The fault lab

16 incidents, from a congested antenna and a long power cut to a fibre cut and a BGP error. Each shows the symptoms a customer sees and the measures an engineer reads; visitors guess the cause, then try a repair. The wrong one is shown not to work, and why.

STEPS

  1. Pick an incident
  2. Answer Diagnostic: which component is at fault
  3. Apply a repair and read the verdict
06

Who is responsible?

A matrix sets out, for operators, CAMTEL, the regulator, the ministry and content providers, when each one is responsible in technical, contractual and regulatory terms, from the texts and public documents consulted, without naming a culprit by default.

STEPS

  1. Read the matrix row by row
  2. Open the legal framework below
  3. Click a reference to see the source
07

Market and reforms

Nine scenarios, from two big operators to open wholesale access and infrastructure sharing, show the effect on price, coverage and operator profit. A two-operator game shows why prices can stay high, and a sensitivity chart says which assumption matters most.

STEPS

  1. Pick a scenario from A to I
  2. Adjust the structure sliders
  3. Compare price and coverage
08

Satellite lab

Low and geostationary orbits drawn to scale, the minimum delay that physics allows for each, and six architectures compared, from fibre to the home to satellite, with a dated regulatory status.

STEPS

  1. Read the minimum delay for each orbit
  2. Compare the six architectures
  3. Check the status and its date
09

Business lab and your own operator

Configure an installation for a site, from users and buildings to power and backup, and get a diagram, a bill of materials and a feasibility report. A second module builds an operator, from a neighbourhood ISP to a national network, over five years: topology, investment, running costs, churn and risks.

STEPS

  1. Open Business Lab or Ton opérateur
  2. Set the site or pick a preset
  3. Copy the report
10

Observatory and sources

The latest verified figures, with their period, method and limits, and a form to record your own speed test. Every figure on the site links to a dated source with a confidence level, and a method page lists what the data does not say and where sources disagree.

STEPS

  1. Open Observatoire
  2. Click a reference such as M-12
  3. Read Méthode for the limits
03Tips
  • Start with your path: the citizen path takes about ten minutes and covers the essentials.
  • Switch to Ingénieur to see formulas, units and how each result is computed.
  • Figures marked as simulations are teaching models, not measurements of a real network.
04FAQ
Is this an official site of ART or MINPOSTEL?

No. It is an independent initiative of Lemon Network Solutions, with no affiliation to the regulator or the ministry.

Are the numbers real?

Facts come from dated public sources, each with its reference. Simulations are labelled as teaching models with their assumptions shown.

Does it blame an operator?

No. Responsibilities are shown as conditions, from the texts consulted, and no motive is claimed without evidence.

Do I need an account?

No. Everything runs in the browser.

Which languages?

French by default, and English.
